chapter: Sidemen, the Hampton years, race and money
title: Nat Hentoff as a classical disc jockey
summary: Mingus claims he got Hentoff into jazz and recalls their letters.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: You talked about -- you said that Nat Hentoff gave you a lot of good press when you needed it. How about people like Leonard Feather, who were --
Nat Hentoff did what? I wasn't listening.
Well, in your book you said that he helped you when you needed somebody to write about you.
I said that in my book?
Yeah, you mentioned Nat Hentoff in your -- said he was -- when you were in New York, he was one of the people who gave you -- wrote a lot about you and said good things about you.

No, in my book, I said -- I got him concerned in jazz. I met him when he was a classical disc jockey in Boston. And I think George Wain had time on the program, but he still wouldn't play any jazz records. I got him into jazz.

I'm pretty sure he'll tell you that. He played only classical -- at home he might have some jazz records, I don't know about that, but it appeared to me that he didn't know anything about jazz. I used to write letters to him. There's A (dable) letter I wrote to him describing what a bass violin will be doing ten years from the time I wrote the letter. And it's just what they're doing right now. Broken lines, broken rhythms.

He asked me what I thought would happen 20 years from now. So we used to write -- each about four letters. REMEMBER Saying -- I don't (inaudible) him, other than the fact he was more avant garde, honest critic. He didn't just write about me, he wrote about a lot of guys that hadn't been written about.
With his knowledge of classical music, you know the way those classical guys talk? I didn't know that much about the music myself. I wonder if he really knew about classical music.
I don't know, because I didn't know anything about it.

That's what he was, a classical disc jockey. Unless he was just doing that for one night. Maybe the night I went there he (inaudible) just playing some classical music, and he was a jazz jockey. I never had no way of knowing.
